b: Infringement procedures have been opened against the four member states for failing to meet requirements on the designation of authorities responsible for enforcing the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which is due to apply from 30 Dec 2026.
The EU Deforestation Regulation aims to prevent commodities and products placed on the European market from contributing to deforestation and forest degradation (Image: Unsplash)

The EU Commission has sent letters of formal notice to Bulgaria, Greece, Malta and Poland for failing to designate competent authorities under the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) and notify the Commission accordingly.
The letters, issued on 19 Nov 2026, mark the opening of infringement procedures against the four member states ahead of the regulation’s application from 30 Dec 2026.

The EUDR aims to ensure that key commodities and products placed on the EU market do not contribute to deforestation or forest degradation, which are major drivers of climate change and biodiversity loss.

Under the regulation, member states were required to designate one or more competent authorities by 30 Dec 2023 and notify the Commission accordingly. These authorities are responsible for overseeing implementation and enforcement, including carrying out checks on operators and traders established in the EU and, where necessary, requiring corrective measures or imposing penalties.

Bulgaria has designated competent authorities for all commodities covered by the EUDR except rubber. Greece, Malta and Poland have either failed to designate the required authorities or notify the Commission of their appointments.

The four member states now have two months to respond and address the shortcomings identified. If their responses are deemed unsatisfactory, the Commission may take the infringement procedures to the next stage.
